q: Polaris is the brightest star in the northern hemisphere night sky.

q: How old is the universe?

q: The moons, Miranda, Ariel, Umbriel, Titania and Oberon orbit which planet?

q: Which of the following spacecraft never touched the moon?

q: To the nearest minute, how long does it take for light to travel from the Sun to the Earth?

q: Which planet did the "Viking 1" spacecraft send surface images of, starting in 1976?

q: Which planet in the Solar System is the closest to the Sun?

q: On which mission did the Space Shuttle Columbia break up upon re-entry?
e: The brave crew flew aboard STS-107, traveling on a science adventure before their tragic journey home.

q: Which of these two plates are best know for forming earthquakes and tsunami's?

q: Centripetal force is an apparent force that acts outward on a body moving around a center, arising from the body's inertia.
e: That is false because centripetal force actually pulls inward, hugging you toward the center like an invisible leash on a spinning ride.

q: El Niño pushes warm water to the coasts of the Western Pacific during winter.
e: This is true because El Niño stirs up the Pacific like a warm bath, shifting tropical currents when winter arrives.

q: Gannymede is the largest moon of which planet?

q: What is the name of the Supermassive Black Hole in the centre of the Milky Way?

q: Which of the following did NOT come from a once-living organism?

q: Our Solar System orbits the center of our Milky Way Galaxy. One full revolution takes about 200-250 million years. The last time our solar system was where it is now, what was occurring here on Earth?

Pangaea (read as: pahn-JEE-ah) was just breaking up into the continents we know today

There were no animals living on land but the seas were full of life

q: Which of the following types of light has the longest wavelength?
e: Infrared waves stretch out long and lazy, carrying cozy heat waves that ripple farther apart than visible colors or snappy X-rays.

q: A 10 kilogram mass hangs from a string in an elevator that is accelerating upwards at 2.0 meters per second squared. What is the tension in the string in newtons?
e: The elevator floor pushes up while gravity pulls down, teaming up so the string feels a tight pull of 118 newtons.

q: Which of the following triples of quantum numbers n, l, m are NOT allowed?
e: When an electron's energy level is one and its shape is zero, its tilt cannot be minus one because only zero is allowed.

q: Which of the following is NOT a true statement about electric and gravitational fields?
a: Both can act in a vacuum
Both are proportional to the product of the quantity that causes the field

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true of buckminsterfullerene [buhk-min-ster-FOOL-uh-reen]?

q: Which of the following provides a measure of the amount of matter in a substance?

q: In which of the following parts of the Milky Way is the solar system located?
e: We cruise along like cozy passengers tucked safely inside one of the Milky Way's glowing, curved spiral arms.

q: What is the primary method used by a reactor operator to reduce the power level in a boiling water nuclear reactor?
a: Addition of water to the reactor vessel
Removal of water from the reactor vessel
e: Sliding control rods into the reactor snatches up zooming neutrons, quietly tucking the runaway heat into a gentle nap.

q: Two objects have the same size and shape but one is twice as heavy as the other. If air resistance is negligible, what happens when they are dropped simultaneously from a building?

They land on the ground at the same time and have the same speed
They land on the ground at the same time but the heavy one has more speed

q: The man-made satellites at the lowest orbits generally orbit at a distance of 150 kilometers above Earth. Which of the following best explains why?
a: At this distance, they feel minimal gravitational attraction to Earth
At this distance, they feel minimal air resistance from Earth's atmosphere
It is impossible to travel fast enough to maintain an orbit below this altitude
This is the height at which geostationary orbits can be maintained

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about hummingbirds?

They may become torpid at night
At their active metabolic rate, they can survive without food for about three days
They have to consume about their body weight in nectar daily

q: Which of the following types of magmas has the greatest percentage of dissolved gas?
e: Rhyolitic magma is super thick and sticky, trapping bubbly gases inside until it is ready to blow!

q: Mars is observed to have a very thin atmosphere compared to Earth. Which of the following statements does NOT help explain this difference?
a: Mars is further from the Sun than Earth
Mars has less geothermal activity than Earth
e: Being farther from the sun keeps gases colder and easier to hold, so distance does not explain Mars's thin atmosphere.

q: What parameter of a planet's orbit is a measure of how closely the orbit approximates a perfect circle?
e: Eccentricity measures how stretched out an orbit is, showing whether a planet loops in a tidy circle or a squished oval.

q: The temperature outside is 85 F and the air is holding a maximum amount of moisture. If the temperature drops rapidly to 65F, which of the following will MOST likely happen:

e: The Euler equations give scientists the clever math recipe to track how swirling water and rushing fluids glide along.

q: Bio Syngas is a synthetic composition of what pair of gases?
e: Bio syngas is a bubbly partnership where carbon monoxide and energetic hydrogen team up to make useful fuel.

q: Which of the following chemical processes combines methane with water to produce hydrogen gas and carbon monoxide?
e: Steam reforming uses a blast of super-hot water vapor to gently break methane apart into useful hydrogen gas and carbon monoxide.

q: Harmonics, an issue of power quality, causes which of the following effects?

Power interruption for more than one minute
e: Harmonics are like mischievous echoes in the wires, twisting and distorting the clean, smooth waves of electricity flowing through a circuit.

q: Which of the following is the term for the phenomenon in which light striking a metal ejects electrons from its atoms?
e: In the photoelectric effect, energetic light beams give shy electrons a playful push, knocking them right out of their metal homes.

q: Which of the following energy sources used in power plants contributes the least to the plants' carbon dioxide emissions?
e: Spinning turbines let the friendly breeze do all the pushing without burning anything, releasing zero dirty carbon dioxide.

q: The purpose of a generator in a power plant is to convert one type of energy into another type. What are these two types of energy?
e: Spinning parts use their moving mechanical energy to stir up buzzing electrical power for our homes.

q: Why are exhaust fans energy efficient cooling mechanisms in early summer months?

Exhaust fans physically pull hot air out of the home
Exhaust fans create a cooling breeze
Exhaust fans create a vacuum that prevents hot air from leaking inside the home
e: An exhaust fan simply whisks stubborn hot air right out the window, ushering cooler breezes inside without wasting power.

q: A comet's gas tail points in which of the following directions?
e: The sun breathes out a fierce solar wind, blowing the comet's glowing gas tail straight away like hair in a giant fan.

q: Which of the following is used to describe a thrust fault?
e: A thrust fault happens when giant slabs of rock squeeze together at a convergent boundary, like two friendly bears hugging too tightly.

q: An observer is watching a train pass. As the train approaches the observer, in what way will the frequency of the sound emanating from the train appear to change relative to the observer?

It exists in a region of the solar system beyond the eight planets

Finding a line that fits a collection of points

Changing light refraction from mixing cool air with warm air

Potential energy is greatest at two different displacements

sound is louder the closer it is to an observer

e: Jupiter and the Sun are cosmic twins, both whipped up from giant swirling clouds of hydrogen and helium gas.

q: Why is it winter in the northern hemisphere when it is summer in the southern hemisphere?
a: The manner in which the Earth rotates regulates the seasons on Earth
The northern hemisphere is tilted away from the Sun when the southern hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun
Because of the Earth's revolution, each hemisphere experiences summer when it is closest to the Sun and winter when it is further away
Because of the Earth's rotation, seasons are regulated by photoperiods
e: Earth tilts like a leaning top, so when the northern half points away from the warm sun, it chills into winter.

q: Which of the following CANNOT be readily used as a source of energy in a fuel cell?
e: A fuel cell drinks hydrogen to make clean power, while oxygen only helps the reaction and cannot be the fuel.

q: Which country has the largest proven coal reserves?
e: Tucked beneath its rolling hills, the United States holds more proven coal than any other country on Earth.

q: Which of the following is closest to the number of astronomical units from the Earth to Proxima Centauri?
e: Visiting our nearest neighbor star takes a trek across about 3 times ten to the fifth astronomical units!

q: A sound wave hits a wall, causing a reflection. Which of the following statements about this reflection is NOT correct?
a: The wave will bounce off the wall
The speed of the wave may change
The frequency of the wave will not change
The amplitude of the wave may change
e: Since the sound bounces right back into the same air, it keeps traveling at the exact same speedy pace.

q: A red ball has a mass of 2 grams and a volume of 8 cubic centimeters. A yellow ball has a mass of 5 grams and a volume of 2 cubic centimeters. When both balls are placed into a bucket of water, which of the following is true?
a: The yellow ball floats and the red ball sinks
The red ball floats and the yellow ball sinks
Both the red and yellow ball float
Both the red and yellow ball sink
e: The airy red ball is lighter than water so it floats, while the packed yellow ball sinks right to the bottom!

q: Scientists supported by the Department of Energy are studying vibrational energy levels in molecules. What region of the electromagnetic spectrum are they using to probe these energy levels?
e: Invisible infrared waves have just the right cozy warmth to make tiny molecules wiggle and dance to a lively beat.

q: Gamma rays released during the Sun's fusion would take thousands of years to reach the Sun's surface from which of the following solar layers?
e: Deep in the Sun's crowded core, tiny rays of light play bumper cars with matter for thousands of years before finally escaping!

q: Which of the following types of stars has the weakest hydrogen Balmer lines?
e: Type G stars are a bit too cool to excite hydrogen strongly, giving them the weakest Balmer lines here.

q: In the U.S., the frequency of alternating current is which of the following cycles per second?
e: Electricity does a lightning-fast dance inside your walls, switching directions sixty times every second to power your favorite toys.

q: Which of the following types of radiation has the greatest ability to penetrate matter?
e: Energetic gamma rays zip straight through matter like unstoppable ghosts, piercing much deeper than chunkier particles ever could.

q: Which of the following has the highest kinetic energy?
a: A 35-gram bullet traveling at 1.20 X 103 meters per second
A 35-kilogram cheetah running at 30 meters per second
An 875-kilogram car traveling at 5 meters per second
A 148-gram pitched baseball moving at 45 meters per second
e: That tiny bullet zooms so blisteringly fast that its incredible speed gives it far more moving energy than even a leaping cheetah.

q: Scientists in the Biosciences Division at Argonne National Lab are studying lignin, a structural polymer. Where can one find lignin?
e: Lignin acts like tough natural glue inside plant cell walls, giving wood the mighty strength to stand tall.

q: Why aren't birds electrified when standing on power lines?
a: Because there is no difference in potential energy when they stand on top of power lines
Because the kinetic energy remains the same
Because there is a differential in potential that allows the flow of energy through them
e: Electricity only flows when there is a difference to jump across. Because a bird's feet share the same energy level, the current safely skips them!

q: A stream is dammed, raising its base level. Which of the following is most likely to happen?
a: The stream deposits sediment upstream of the dam
The gradient of the stream increases
e: When a dam blocks the way, the sleepy stream slows down and drops its heavy load of sandy sediment upstream.

q: Which of the following units is used to measure electric current:
e: Amperes measure the lively river of electric charge marching through a wire, telling us how much electricity is zooming by.

q: Which of the following is the most efficient type of solar cell?
e: Multijunction cells stack different layers to catch many colors of sunlight at once, making them the most efficient light-catching champions around.

q: What term describes the height of an object in the sky?
e: Altitude tells stargazers exactly how high an object sits above the horizon in our vast night sky.

q: Imagine evenly spaced radial lines emanating from a point source that represents the Earth. If 9 force lines pass through a plane x meters from the source, how many force lines pass through a plane of the same size 3x meters away?
e: As lines fan outward, stepping three times farther away spreads them nine times thinner, leaving just one line passing through.

q: Hydroelectric energy accounts for which of the following approximate proportions of the total energy consumed annually in the United States?
e: Rushing river water spins mighty turbines to power our homes, supplying about eight percent of all the energy our country uses.

q: Which of the following changes will NOT increase the efficiency of a dehumidifier?
a: Higher surface area of the coils
A higher coefficient of performance on the compressor
e: A dehumidifier needs ice-cold coils to catch sticky water drops, so making that evaporator warmer stops it from doing its chilly job.

q: In general, an object's de Broglie [da-BROY] wavelength is inversely proportional to which of the following of its properties?
e: The more momentum a zooming particle packs, the shorter and tighter its tiny de Broglie wavelength becomes.

q: A rising barometer and clear skies indicate an approaching:
e: Heavy, high-pressure air gently presses down on the clouds, shooing them away to leave bright, clear skies.

q: Coal is primarily used to generate electricity. Which of the following is the second largest use of coal?
e: After making electricity, coal is baked red-hot in giant furnaces to melt iron rocks into shiny steel for skyscrapers!

q: Earth reflects approximately 30% of the light it receives from the Sun back into space. Which of the following components of Earth is responsible for the predominant portion of this reflectivity?
e: Fluffy white clouds act like giant mirrors floating in the sky, bouncing most of Earth's reflected sunlight straight back into space.

q: What is the term for the maximum slope angle that a pile of loose sediment can sustain without falling or rolling downward?
e: The angle of repose is a sandcastle's tipping point, showing how steep loose grains can pile before tumbling down.

q: An object is placed 10 centimeters from a double convex lens with a focal length of 20 centimeters. Which of the following types of image will be produced?
e: Because the object sits inside the focal point, the lens creates an upright, virtual image, just like looking through a magnifying glass.

q: Which of the following activities will increase your carbon footprint?
a: Eating a more local vegetarian diet
Keeping your family's car tires inflated to the correct level
Using public transportation like buses and trains
e: Raising cattle takes lots of land and food, plus burping cows release potent methane gas that puffs up your footprint.

q: Halley's Comet, a famous short-period comet, was last visible from Earth in 1986. In which of the following years will it be visible from Earth again?
e: This snowy space traveler takes seventy-five years to loop around the sun, meaning its next glowing visit arrives in 2061.

q: Two objects, each with a mass of 1 kilogram, are moving directly towards each other at 20 meters per second before they collide perfectly inelastically. What will be the impulse in kilogram meters per second on the first object?
e: When the speedy objects crash and stick together, they stop completely. Stopping that one-kilogram object at twenty meters per second takes an impulse of twenty!

q: The rings of Saturn are primarily composed of which of the following?
a: Hydrogen, helium, methane and other trace gases
e: Saturn wears a dazzling, sparkling hula hoop made almost entirely of floating lumps of chilly water ice.

q: Which of the following represents the rate at which atmospheric gases and particles are moved across a surface?
e: Flux is the neat word for a busy parade of air and dust rushing across a surface.

q: Which of the following types of quantities appears in a free-body diagram?
e: These clever little sketches draw arrows to show every single push and pull, or force, nudging an object around.

q: Which of the following are the two parts of sunspots?
e: Every sunspot wears a dark, cozy center called an umbra, wrapped in a lighter, shaded blanket called the penumbra.

q: The typical thunderstorm clouds of summer, sometimes referred to as hammerheads or thunderheads, are called:
e: Towering cumulonimbus clouds puff up tall like giant anvil castles in the sky, brewing up dramatic rumbles of thunder.

q: What is the primary element in today's commercially available solar cells?
e: Silicon is the busy worker inside solar panels, soaking up bright sunshine like a sponge and turning it into clean electricity!

q: Which of the following is NOT true of humidity:
a: relative humidity is a description of the water vapor content in air
humans feel uncomfortable when the relative humidity is high because cooling from sweating is less effective
dew points normally occur when the relative humidity of an air mass is 100%
the dew point is measured in percent along with the relative humidity
e: While humidity loves percentages, dew point is actually a temperature, proudly wearing degrees like your morning forecast.

q: Which of the following is NOT an important component of the hydrologic cycle?
e: Clouds, rain, and soil carry Earth's giant water highway, making our personal breathing, called respiration, too tiny to be a main part.

q: Two ores of iron are hematite and magnetite. They can be identified on the basis of the streak test. What color is the hematite streak and what color is the magnetite streak, respectively?
e: When scratched like chalk, rusty hematite leaves a reddish orange scribble, while magnetic magnetite draws in bold black.

q: Of the following choices, which one best describes the way snowflakes form?
a: Water vapor freezes onto ice crystals inside clouds
Ice attaches to dust particles in the air
e: Floating water vapor hugs tiny ice crystals in chilly clouds, growing into beautiful, delicate frozen stars.

q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the Tampa Bay desalination plant?
a: It can produce up to 25 million gallons of drinking water per day
It uses the process of reverse osmosis to produce drinking water from saltwater
Concentrated seawater is directed back to the power plant, where it is mixed with cooling water and returned to the Bay
Increased salinity in Tampa Bay is a proven environmental hazard of this operation
e: The plant safely dilutes its leftover salty water, so extra saltiness has never actually been proven to harm the bay's happy fish.

q: Which of the following is the most common type of galaxy in the universe?
e: Smooth elliptical galaxies shape up like giant, glowing cosmic footballs, and they outnumber every other kind of galaxy in our starry universe.

q: What type of nebula consists primarily of hot, ionized gas that radiates light?
e: An emission nebula is like a giant cosmic neon sign, glowing with its own colorful light as hot gas gets excited.

q: Which of the following BEST explains why a concrete floor feels colder than a wooden floor if both are at 21C:
a: wood is not as dense as concrete
concrete conducts heat better than wood
wood is alive and concrete is not
concrete is much less elastic than wood
e: Concrete is a speedy heat thief, whisking warmth right out of your bare feet much faster than cozy wood can.

q: Which of the following cloud types is most commonly associated with major thunderstorms?
e: Cumulonimbus clouds billow up like giant, dark sky castles, brewing up rumbling thunder and flashy lightning.

q: Researchers at Fermi National Accelerator Lab are designing a new kind of qubit [Q-bit]. Which of the following best describes the difference between a qubit and a classical bit?
a: Qubits use quantum tunneling to move data more quickly
Qubits can exist in a superposition of classical states
Qubits exploit quantum interference to become more energy efficient than classical bits
Qubits use quantum decoherence to simulate multiple classical bits
e: Unlike normal bits that choose one or zero, playful qubits can dance between both numbers at the very same time.

q: The efficiency of a solar water heater collector depends directly on solar irradiance and which of the following?
a: Collector temperature and efficiency of the heat exchanger
Efficiency of the heat exchanger and temperature of the water
Tilt angle of the collector and collector temperature
e: A heater's efficiency depends on how warm it gets compared to the chilly outside air trying to steal its heat away.

q: Territorial waters are defined as extending how many nautical miles from a shoreline?
e: A country's ocean backyard stretches exactly twelve nautical miles from shore, giving coastal nations their very own watery kingdom to look after.

q: Government agencies and utilities offer various incentives to encourage people to improve the energy efficiency of buildings and vehicles. Which of the following is NOT a typical incentive?
e: While programs happily offer tax breaks or cash back, they rarely send workers to do the actual hardware installation for you.

q: Soundtracks of space movies frequently have sounds of ships exploding or whizzing through space. Why is this an inaccurate depiction of space?
a: Sound waves are distorted in space so everything would sound like it was under water
Sound cannot travel through a vacuum
Everything would have a very high pitch in space
Space vibrations would muffle the explosions
e: Space is an empty vacuum with no air molecules to bump together, leaving rocket zooms completely, beautifully silent.

q: What happens to the wavelength and frequency of a wave when the amplitude of a wave increases?
e: Growing taller just makes a wave bigger, leaving its marching speed and spacing happily unchanged.

q: Which of the following is associated with Karst topography?
e: When sneaky underground water dissolves soft rock, the ground suddenly gives way into giant hollow pockets called sinkholes.

q: According to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, construction of communications towers may negatively impact migratory birds. Which of the following is LEAST dangerous to migrating birds ?
a: Lighted towers with a height greater than 199 feet
Unlighted towers with a height greater than 199 feet
Lighted towers with a height less than 199 feet
Unlighted towers with a height less than 199 feet
e: Short towers without confusing, glowing lights stay out of the birds' way, letting feathered travelers zoom safely through the night!

q: Which of the following is a neutron moderator?
e: Ordinary water acts like a gentle cushion, playfully bumping into speedy neutrons to slow them down.

q: Which of the following forms of winter precipitation is most likely to cause downed power lines and broken tree limbs:
e: Freezing rain glazes trees and wires in thick, heavy coats of shiny ice until the branches snap under all that extra weight!

q: Why do the planets Uranus and Neptune appear blue?
a: Their atmospheres absorb blue light very efficiently.
The wind speeds are very high and so show a strong blue shift.
Their surfaces are covered with water and their clouds are very thin.
Their atmospheres absorb red light very efficiently.
e: Methane gas in their skies hungrily gulps down red sunlight, leaving only lovely, icy blue rays to bounce back to our eyes.

q: Radiocarbon dating is a commonly used technique for determining the age of organic material. Which of the following numbers is closest to the age, in years, after which organic material is unsuitable for carbon dating?
e: After about 50,000 years, a fossil runs out of its special ticking carbon, leaving no clues behind for scientists to count.

q: Which of the following kinds of power plants is BEST suited for peak load demands?
e: When everyone turns on lights at once, gas turbines can fire up in minutes like speedy race cars to meet the sudden peak demand.

q: Faraday's law of induction most directly states which of the following relationships?
a: A static magnetic field generates an electric field
A static electric field generates a magnetic field
A changing magnetic field generates an electric field
A changing electric field generates a magnetic field
e: When a magnetic field moves and changes, it magically wakes up an electric field to get power flowing!

q: Electrical current is best conducted through which of the following substances?
e: Copper has friendly, loose electrons that pass electric sparks along in a super-fast relay race, making it a wonderful conductor.

q: Analysts at Los Alamos National Laboratory have shown how to minimize environmental impacts by refracturing shale gas wells. Which of the following is not an environmental benefit of refracturing?
a: Fewer wells need to be drilled
Natural gas is more efficiently removed from each well
Carbon dioxide is deposited in a form of carbon sequestration
Natural gas does not release harmful byproducts
e: Even though refracturing saves wells, burning natural gas still puffs out pollution, so it definitely produces harmful byproducts.

q: Which of the following is not a type of heat pump?
e: Heat pumps love moving warmth from air, water, or soil, but radiant systems just glow heat straight from cozy floors instead of pumping it.

q: What is the metric unit for mass?
e: When the metric system weighs a heavy backpack or a playful puppy, it measures their mass in kilograms.

q: Models are frequently employed in science. Which of the following is not true of scientific models?
a: They cannot be changed once formalized
They are patterned after items or events in the natural world
They offer a means of testing predictions
e: Science is a growing adventure, so when curious researchers find new clues, they happily update their models instead of freezing them forever.

q: Which of the following characteristics are exhibited by biota that occur early in the succession of a region?
e: The first brave little plants to settle empty land grow super fast, showing high productivity as they turn sunlight into life.

q: Which of the following is a characteristic of a turbidite?
a: Found in alkaline bodies of water
e: When underwater avalanches settle, the heaviest pebbles sink first and tiny grains rest on top, leaving behind neat graded bedding layers.

q: Utilities distribute electrical power at high voltage from generating plants to industrial and residential customers through a network of wires. Which of the following is the term for these wires?
e: Tall transmission lines act like giant highway lanes, zooming energetic electricity across miles right into our cozy neighborhoods.

q: What is the number one tip the Department of Energy has for homeowners to save money on energy bills?
a: Lower the temperature on your water heater
Use a power strip for your electronic equipment
Use natural lighting rather than artificial
Install and set a programmable thermostat
e: A programmable thermostat acts like a smart little buddy, turning down the heat while you sleep so your house saves the most energy.

q: A perfectly efficient engine would transform the chemical energy in gasoline into:
e: In an ideal world with zero wasted heat, every drop of fuel energy would turn directly into useful work!

q: A low-e window will have greater performance in comparison to a standard home window in what regard?
a: It will allow more infrared energy into the home
It will allow less ultraviolet energy into the home
It will emit less radiant energy from the home
It will allow more visible light into the home
e: These clever windows wear a microscopic coat that bounces warmth back inside, keeping cozy radiant heat from sneaking outdoors.

q: Reverse and normal faults are both examples of what general type of fault?
e: Dip-slip faults let rock slabs slide up or down an inclined slope, just like normal and reverse faults love to do.

q: Your teacher asks you to draw a free body diagram of a box being moved by a rope and pulley system. Which of the following should be included?
a: All forces acting on the box
All forces exerted by the box on itself
All forces exerted by the box on other objects
Both forces for all action-reaction pairs
e: Picture the box as the star of the show; you only draw the pushes and pulls acting directly on it.

q: To maximize the concentration of energy from the Sun, heliostats must do which of the following?
a: Track the zenith angle of the Sun
Track the solar declination of the Sun
Track the azimuth angle and the altitude of the Sun
Keep the panel facing up at all times
e: These clever mirrors track the Sun's azimuth angle and altitude, following it across the sky like sunflowers to catch every ray.

q: What is the major component of crude oil, by weight?
e: Deep underground, crude oil is mostly made of ring-shaped molecules called naphthenes, giving this thick liquid its heavy weight.

q: Which of the following stars can someone in North America see year-round?
e: Polaris sits faithfully above our spinning North Pole, shining bright all year long without ever dipping beneath the horizon.

q: Scientists working at Ames Laboratory have devised a way to increase the catalytic activity of nanoparticles in fuel cell applications. What quantity related to the particles did scientists focus on increasing?
e: Giving tiny particles more surface area creates extra playground space on the outside for chemical reactions to meet and happen faster.

q: In which of the following states would you be more likely to find a methane digester on a farm or ranch?
e: Wisconsin is packed with dairy cows, so its farms use special digesters to turn smelly manure into bright, clean energy.

q: Approximately what percent of Earth's water is in the form of ice?
e: Most water fills deep oceans, leaving only about 1.6 percent locked away as shimmering glaciers and frozen polar caps.

q: In a 24 hour period, when does the coldest temperature of the day typically occur:
e: The ground leaks warmth all night long, making the air shiver at its coldest right after sunrise.

q: The time required for the Moon to return to the same position relative to the background stars (as seen from Earth) is about how long?
e: Our faithful Moon takes about a month to dance entirely around the sky and return to the very same twinkling star.

q: Which of the following energies is harnessed by floating generators?
e: Floating generators bob happily on rolling ocean waves, turning every bobbing splash into clean, usable electricity.

q: The amount of CO2 produced from burning natural gas will be what percent of the CO2 produced from burning coal, for the same amount of energy output?
e: Natural gas burns far cleaner than lumpy coal, puffing out only about 50 percent as much carbon dioxide to make the same energy.

q: Six tidal barrage power plants are currently operating throughout the world. Which of the following nations leads the world in installed tidal energy capacity?
e: South Korea puts the tides to work best, leading the whole world in catching rushing ocean water to make clean electricity.

q: Assuming the potential difference remains constant, if the resistance of a circuit is doubled, which of the following will happen to the power dissipation?
a: It will decrease by a fourth
e: When a wire makes electricity work twice as hard to squeeze through, the power flowing through gets cut right in half.

q: Mass wasting occurs when what pair of forces become unbalanced?
e: A hillside stays still until greedy gravity pulls harder than sleepy friction can hold on, sending rocks tumbling down!

q: Which of the following can occur with light but NOT sound?
e: Light waves can do a special dance called polarization by lining up their wiggles, but sound waves simply cannot.

q: Which of the following sound wave frequencies in hertz would a human be most likely to hear?
e: Our ears are built best for middle pitches, making a bright one-thousand-hertz hum delightfully easy for us to hear.

q: Which of the following types of sediment deposits are formed primarily by wind processes?
e: Whenever playful winds scoop up dust and sculpt swirling desert dunes, geologists call those breezy sand piles eolian deposits.

q: At the Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory, part of the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, scientists are examining the formation of soot using jet fuel. How is soot formed?
e: When fuel does not get enough air to burn completely, messy leftover carbon gathers into dark, smoky flakes of soot.

q: Which of the following equations represents Dalton's law?
a: V1/n1 = V2/n2 [V 1 over n 1 equals V 2 over n 2]
e: Dalton showed that mixed gases share their room politely, simply adding up each little push to make the total pressure!

q: A reaction where the system absorbs energy is known as which of the following?
e: An endothermic reaction acts like a thirsty sponge for heat, greedily soaking up surrounding energy to make things chilly.

q: Which of the following is farthest from the Sun?
e: Way past Neptune and icy dwarf worlds, the giant Oort Cloud floats farthest away, like a snowy bubble wrapped around our solar system.

q: The Moon is full on September 7, 2006. On which of the following days that month will a last quarter Moon occur:
e: The moon loves a steady rhythm, taking about one week to shrink from full to a last quarter, landing right on the 14th.

q: When designing a solar panel field in the northern hemisphere, in what cardinal direction should the panels tilt to collect the greatest solar energy collection?
e: Because the sun arcs across the southern sky up north, solar panels tilt south to catch every golden ray.

q: Theoretically, an absolute maximum of how many ATP molecules can be produced from the complete oxidation of one glucose molecule through aerobic respiration?
e: By squeezing every drop of energy from a single sugar molecule, a busy cell can craft up to 38 little ATP batteries.

q: Which of the following explains why the same side of the Moon always faces the Earth?
a: The Moon is tidally locked to the Earth
The Moon rotates around its axis once every 12 hours
The Moon rotates around its axis once every 24 hours
The Moon is gravitationally uncoupled from the Earth
e: Earth's gentle gravity slowed the Moon's spin until it matched its orbit, locking its smiling face toward us forever.

q: Marcellus shale occurs in the subsurface under several states. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
e: While this underground rock blanket stretches across nearby states, it stops short before ever tucking under Indiana.

q: Which of the following BEST describes how the SI unit called the Newton is derived:
a: the product of force times time
the energy in one kilogram traveling at one meter per second
the force needed to accelerate 1 kilogram at one meter per second squared
the power needed to accelerate 1 kilogram at one kilometer per hour
e: A single newton is the exact friendly shove needed to speed up a one-kilogram mass by one meter per second squared!

q: In a standard lithium-ion battery, from what substance is the anode made?
e: Inside the battery, tiny lithium travelers nestle happily into sheets of carbon, making it the perfect home for the anode.

q: In a fast nuclear reactor, why would coolant other than water be needed?
a: Water cannot be used with the fast nuclear turbines
e: Speedy neutrons must stay fast to do their jobs, but water bumps into them and slows them right down.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT part of the standard model of frictional force assumptions?
a: Frictional force is independent of contact area
Frictional force is proportional to normal force
Frictional coefficient is proportional to force between objects
Frictional force is independent of velocity
e: How slippery two surfaces are depends only on what they are made of, not on how hard they press together.

q: Fermi National Lab scientists studied the creation of a top quark by a collision of a proton and an anti-proton. Which of the following particles is created concomitantly [Kon-koh-MIT-ent-lee] in order to obey conservation laws?
e: Nature loves perfect balance, so whenever a heavy top quark pops into existence, its anti-top twin must appear beside it!

q: Which of the following describes when flooding is most likely to occur as the result of a slow moving, relatively long term, moderate rain event?
a: After it has been raining for about an hour
After it has been raining for a few hours
At the beginning of the rainstorm
e: The ground drinks slowly, so rainwater takes hours to creep into rivers and cause flooding only after the storm finishes.

q: In which of the following cases will the displacement of the object be the least?
a: A 1.2-kilogram object moving 4 meters up an incline of 45 degrees
A 3.1-kilogram object moving 3 meters on a flat surface
A 0.5-kilogram object moving 6 meters along a circle with circumference 6 meters
Cannot be determined from the information given
e: Traveling all the way around a circle brings you right back where you started, making your final displacement zero!

q: Currently, almost all used nuclear fuel from power plants in the U.S. is stored at which of the following?
e: Used fuel stays right at home where it was made, resting safely in heavy steel casks at the power plant.

q: The Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission (TRMM) satellite was launched in 1997 with the primary mission of measuring rainfall from space using passive microwave and active radar sensors. Which of the following is NOT a benefit of TRMM?
a: Increased understanding of the water cycle
Increased understanding of the heat release associated with rainfall
Better likelihood of accurate climate models
e: This storm-watching satellite focused on tropical rain clouds down below, not the wispy airplane exhaust trails known as contrails.

q: Which of the following choices is NOT a condition required for the formation of a thunderstorm?
a: Humid air in low- to mid-troposphere
e: Thunderstorms are cozy heat-lovers, so they crave warm air to cook up giant storms instead of low, chilly temperatures!

q: Scientists using the Advanced Photon Source have solved the structure of the glucagon [GLUE-kah-gon] receptor, providing a potential therapeutic target for what disease?
e: Glucagon helps control the body's sweet sugar levels, so understanding it gives doctors a powerful key to treat diabetes.

q: As of 2014, which of the following countries generates the largest percentage of its electricity using nuclear power?
e: Among these nations, snowy Sweden relied on nuclear power for about forty percent of its electricity, taking the crown in 2014.

q: Which of the following types of stars is expected to last for the longest time in its current stage of stellar evolution?
e: Tiny red dwarf stars sip their fuel so gently that they can keep glowing for trillions of peaceful years.

q: Scientists at SLAC [slack] are using the Linac [LIH-nak] Coherent Light Source to study protein crystal structures. Which of the following best describes a main challenge to this approach?
a: Some proteins crystallize into structures too large to study
e: Some wiggly proteins are just too floppy to freeze into neat crystal blocks for their big science photo shoots.

q: Which of the following is closest to the power required to run a dishwasher?
e: Scrubbing your dirtiest plates takes a hearty burst of about one thousand watts to heat and splash all that water.

q: Which of the following best describes what meteorologists call a mesoscale convective complex:
a: a widespread area of cool, clear conditions
e: A mesoscale convective complex is just a giant neighborhood of thunderstorms teaming up into one huge, rumbling rain party!

q: The best evidence for the model of Earth's interior comes from the study of:
e: Seismology listens to earthquake waves traveling underground, using those deep echoes to draw a map of our planet's hidden heart.

q: Which of the following is not true of seawater?
a: Seawater is denser than fresh water
The freezing point of seawater decreases as salt concentration increases
Seawater is uniformly saline throughout the world
The thermal conductivity of seawater decreases with increasing salinity
e: Our big blue oceans mix constantly, so saltiness varies from place to place rather than staying uniformly the same everywhere.

q: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) classifies physical constants into various categories. Which of the following is NOT considered a universal physical constant?
a: Speed of light in a vacuum
e: Universal constants never change anywhere, but an alpha particle is just a tiny bundle of parts, not a fundamental cosmic constant.

q: Which of the following resulted in petroleum?
a: Dead organisms packed together for millions of years
e: Long ago, microscopic critters settled underground, and millions of years of cozy squishing baked them into rich petroleum.

q: The spectrum of electromagnetic energy emitted by a black body is determined by which of the following?
a: A combination of material and size
e: A black body does not care what it is made of; only its temperature decides what colorful light it glows!

q: Scientists at Fermi National Accelerator Lab working on the Dark Energy Survey have measured a cosmological quantity to be 0.776, with a standard error of 0.017. Assuming normality, which of the following best describes their claim?
a: The value of the quantity definitely lies between 0.759 and 0.793
Throughout the universe, the value of the quantity fluctuates between 0.759 and 0.793
With a probability of 68%, the value of the quantity lies between 0.759 and 0.793
Their instruments recorded a value of 0.776, but they know the instrument can make errors of up to 0.017

q: The mass of most distant stars is estimated by astronomers by measuring which of the following?
a: The speed at which a star is rotating on its axis
The distance between Earth and the star
The gravitation attraction of the star and nearby planetary objects
The speed of light traveling from that star to Earth
e: Astronomers watch how a star's invisible gravitational hug pulls on nearby orbiting objects to figure out just how heavy it is.

q: You installed a brand new Energy Star-rated range in your kitchen, and you discover that it has an induction cooktop. Which of the following cookware materials would best function on an induction cooktop?
e: Induction stoves use magnetic magic to cook, so heavy cast iron pans heat right up because magnets love sticking to iron!

q: What component of the Milky Way galaxy is comprised of a roughly spherical collection of stars and star clusters with almost no gas or dust?
e: The halo wraps around our galaxy like a giant, starry bubble, holding ancient clusters without any messy dust clouds.

q: On a rolling bicycle wheel, which of the following parts of the wheel has the highest instantaneous speed relative to the ground?
a: The forward-most edge of the wheel
e: As a wheel rolls, its top zooms forward twice as fast as the bike itself, while the bottom briefly hugs the ground!

q: Which of the following types of clouds would be most predictive of heavy rain?
e: Towering cumulonimbus clouds puff up like giant, shadowy castles, holding tons of heavy rain ready to pour down.

q: Newton's law of cooling states that which of the following is true?
a: The rate at which the temperature of an object changes can be determined if the difference between the temperature of the body and the ambient temperature is known
A wire heats up whenever current passes through it
All molecular movement ceases at -100 Celsius
A circuit cools down as long as the wires attached to it have a specific number of turns
e: A piping-hot soup cools down faster in a chilly room because the temperature difference sets the cooling pace.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about Tesla coils?
a: They take DC current and step it up to extremely high voltages
Voltages are discharged in the form of electrical arcs
They can create powerful electric fields
Some Tesla coils can wirelessly light up fluorescent lights up to 50 feet away
e: Tesla coils actually run on wiggling AC power, not steady DC, to unleash their dancing sparks!

q: Which of the following is closest to the percentage of mass in our Solar System belonging to the Sun?
e: Our blazing sun is such an enormous heavyweight that it hogs ninety-nine percent of our solar system's entire mass.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the solar tower, Solar Two?
a: It generated steam directly from water in its receiver
It could supply electric power on demand to the local utility company
Nearly 2000 heliostats reflected sunlight onto a receiver located at the top of the tower
Concentrated sunlight heated molten salt to temperatures as high as 1000 Fahrenheit
e: Solar Two caught the blazing sunlight using molten salt first, rather than boiling water directly into steam inside its tower receiver.

q: The Doppler effect occurs:
e: Whether traveling through water, air, or empty space, every single kind of wave stretches or squishes with the Doppler effect.

q: What class of mollusks [MOL-uhsks] includes modern day clams?
e: Clams keep their soft little bodies safe inside two matching shell doors, which makes them proud bivalves!

q: Which of the following could be a likely location for a salt mine?
e: When desert lake water evaporates under the blazing sun, it leaves behind a flat playa coated in thick, mineable salt.

q: Which of the following situations produces the MOST power?
a: 160 newton force acting over 20 meters in 32 seconds
160 newton force acting over 2 meters in 3.2 seconds
16 newton force acting over 20 meters in 3.2 seconds
16 newton force acting over 200 meters in 3.2 seconds

q: In the most common type of geothermal power plant, what rotates the turbines?
e: Deep underground heat boils water into whistling steam that rushes up to spin giant electric turbines.

q: In meteorology, what is another name for a region of high pressure?
e: An anticyclone is like a giant, happy bubble of heavy air, gently pushing clouds away to bring sunny skies.

q: Which of the following is most closely related to the frequency of a wave?
e: Frequency counts how many wave crests roll by, which directly matches how long each individual wave stretches out.

q: A modern camera allows light to hit its sensor through a circular opening called an aperture. Assuming the amount of light per area is uniform; by what factor must the radius of the aperture be multiplied to double the amount of light hitting the sensor?
e: Because a circle's area squares its radius, widening the radius by the square root of two lets in exactly double the light.

q: Astronauts in the space shuttle are about 100 miles above the earth's surface. What is true about the effect of gravity on these space shuttle astronauts?
a: The astronauts are far outside the earth's gravitational field
The astronauts have some mass, but it is less than their mass would be on the earth's surface
The astronauts experience "apparent weightlessness" because they are constantly falling around the earth
The astronauts have no mass as they are orbiting the earth
e: Astronauts float because they are actually in a nonstop, magical free fall around Earth, with gravity gently tugging them along.

q: Which of the following stars is located closest to the north celestial pole?
e: Polaris stays steady in the night sky, sitting almost perfectly above Earth's North Pole to guide wandering travelers home.

q: The energy used in our households comes through electrical lines originating from which of the following locations?
e: A generation station is the buzzing powerhouse where electricity is made before it travels through wires right into your home.

q: Ames National Lab scientists are developing nanoparticles that replace the catalyst in fuel cells. This catalyst is composed of what expensive element?
e: Platinum is a super shiny and crazy expensive metal, so scientists want cheaper ingredients to speed up fuel reactions.

q: What highly efficient technology is currently employed to allow satellites to maintain their orbits without carrying large quantities of fuel?
e: Ion thrusters gently puff out glowing, charged particles to push satellites along on whisper-quiet space journeys with almost no fuel!

q: Scientists supported by the Department of Energy are studying matter whose properties can be described using the Dirac [dih-RAHK] equation. In that sense, this matter is similar to which of the following elementary particles?
e: The Dirac equation describes true matter particles that spin, making the tiny up quark a perfect match.

q: Complex carbohydrates are called:
e: Think of polysaccharides as giant conga lines of tiny sugar friends holding hands to store lots of energy!

q: Which of the following is closest to the number of commercial nuclear reactors currently operating in the United States?
e: Across the country, about one hundred busy nuclear reactors hum day and night to keep our cities glowing bright.

q: Which of the following criteria is most important in determining if a lens is converging or diverging?
a: The thickness of its center compared to its edges

q: Why is it best to hit a baseball on the sweet spot of a bat?
a: There is less friction on the sweet spot
The sweet spot is the widest part of the bat so it easier to hit the ball
When the ball hits the sweet spot more force is imparted to it
Less energy is lost to bat vibrations when the ball hits the sweet spot

q: What is the SI base unit of temperature?
e: Scientists everywhere pick Kelvin as their grand champion base unit to measure how warm or chilly things are.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about arch bridges?
a: Its structure distributes compression through its entire form
Weight is diverted onto its abutments
The curve of the arch reduces the effects of tension
Each half-arch has its own structural integrity

q: Which of the following areas of the United States has the most potential for geothermal energy?

q: What is the primary reason for irradiating food?
a: To make the food taste better
To increase the shelf life of food
To kill pathogens in the food
To make the food more interesting visually
e: Helpful rays zap away sneaky bad germs hiding in your food, keeping every delicious bite safe and healthy.

q: Which of the following sets of two locations have the most similar latitudes?
a: New York City, New York and London, England
Death Valley, California and Boston, Massachusetts
e: Sunny Tampa and snowy Kathmandu sit on nearly the same line across our spinning globe, sharing matching latitudes like faraway neighborhood twins.

q: When a ball rolls downhill, the gravitational potential energy of the ball is transformed into what type of energy?
e: As the ball tumbles down the hill, its stored waiting energy joyfully turns into kinetic energy, the wonderful energy of motion!

q: In years, which of the following is closest to the age of the solar system?
e: Our cozy planetary neighborhood has been dancing around the Sun for about five billion grand birthdays.

q: Which of the following types of coal has the highest carbon content?
e: After baking under giant mountains for eons, hard, shiny anthracite coal holds the highest carbon of any coal.

q: Researchers at Ames National Lab discovered a zinc-platinum catalytic particle that achieves what desirable pairing of physical properties?
e: Like a crinkled leaf, these particles have high surface area to touch things quickly while keeping their volume small.

q: Matilda plays an instrument which produces a higher pitch than the instrument her friend Matt plays. What can we say about the sound waves of Matilda's music?

Both Matilda and Matt's sound waves have the same wavelength, but Matilda's travel slower
Matilda's wave peaks are closer together than Matt's
Both Matilda and Matt's sound waves have the same wavelength, but Matilda's travel faster

q: Which of the following electromagnetic waves has a shorter wavelength than visible light?
e: Ultraviolet waves squeeze closer together than rainbow colors, carrying extra energy beyond what our eyes can see.

q: If you double the mass of a cart while it is undergoing a constant unbalanced force, the acceleration will be:
e: Stuffing twice the weight into the cart makes it twice as stubborn, cutting its pickup speed right in half!

q: Scientists at Sandia National Lab are testing to see if electrical stimulation can improve working memory and reasoning skills. What cortex of the brain are they stimulating?
e: Your prefrontal cortex acts like the wise captain behind your forehead, steering your thoughts, memories, and clever choices.

q: What geologic dating technique measures radioactive decay caused during the shattering of a nucleus by cosmic rays on the surface of an exposed rock?
e: Cosmogenic dating clocks the secret sunburn rocks get when tiny cosmic rays from outer space zap their surface atoms.

q: Which of the following are the highest of the clouds in the troposphere and are composed entirely of ice crystals:

e: Big busy factories in the industrial sector work around the clock, gobbling up more energy than anywhere else.

One continuous sheet of silicon with a backing of metal-conducting material
Lots of individual PV cells that have a backing of metal-conducting material
Strips of silicon form the PV cells that have a backing of metal-conducting material

e: A flat mirror bounces light straight back, showing an upright image that looks real but is truly virtual behind the glass.

e: Scientists brew pond algae for zooming planes and speedy cars, not for quietly warming basements as home heating oil.

q: Which of the following is a unit for sound intensity level?
e: Whether it is a tiny mouse squeak or a roaring rocket, decibels measure just how loud sound energy can be!

q: Which of the following is closest to the ratio of the surface temperature of Aldebaran, a red giant, to that of the Sun?
e: Even though the giant star Aldebaran is huge, its cooler surface is only about half as hot as our Sun!

e: By teaming up to catch invisible signals floating in the air, these tiny electric parts can build a working AM radio!

$1 per kilowatt and $0.10 per kilowatt hour

$3 per kilowatt and $0.10 per kilowatt hour

q: Which of the following is the most common and likely source of exposure to harmful radiation for most people?
a: Discovering a piece of abandoned equipment from the nuclear industry
Exposure to a spent fuel rod
Living near a nuclear power plant
e: Naturally occurring radon gas sneaks up through rock into our homes, making it the most common radiation we meet each day.

e: Porosity just measures how much empty space hides inside a rock, so whether those little pockets connect only controls how easily water flows.

e: X-rays love bouncing off solids because their neat, orderly rows of frozen atoms stand still for a picture!

q: Which of the following is true about sound perception?

The frequency of sound is logarithmically related to the intensity
The loudness of a sound is logarithmically related to the intensity
Sounds measured in decibels are independent of the threshold of hearing

e: Dry air loves to tumble downward near latitude thirty, baking the land into sunny, sandy deserts.

e: Climb five and a half kilometers high, and half of Earth's heavy air blanket is already resting below your boots!

q: Brookhaven National Lab is researching how to tether catalysts to chromophores for artificial photosynthesis. Which of the following is most similar in function to a chromophore?

A natural particle from space that survives impact with the Earth's surface

Becomes a solid above the freezing point
e: Sometimes very quiet water forgets to freeze, staying a liquid even below its normal freezing point!

e: Even when squishing cars lose bouncing energy during a messy crash, their total moving punch, called momentum, is never lost.

the potential energy of the bottle decreases
the potential energy of the bottle increases
the total potential energy of the bottle remains the same

They consume 20-30% less energy than required by federal standards
They convert 30% of the electrical energy into mechanical energy
They have an energy loss of around 20-30%

e: The Sun is so sizzling hot that its atoms dance apart into a wild, glowing soup called plasma!

It is part of the Columbia Basin Project, which irrigates more than 600,000 acres of land
It contains nearly 12 million cubic yards of concrete

e: Deep at the Sun's fiery heart, temperatures roar up to an unbelievable twenty-seven million degrees Fahrenheit!

e: When the wind throws a mighty temper tantrum at level eight, sailors call that roaring blow a gale!

e: Plucky little Landsat 5 kept snapping Earth photos for nearly twenty-nine glorious years, outlasting every other satellite sister!

e: In one year, a speedy ray of light zooms across an astonishing 9.461 trillion kilometers of cosmic space!

e: When bright sunshine tickles your eyes, this funny reflex makes your nose explode with a giant sneeze!

e: Saturn's giant moon Titan snuggles under a cozy, thick blanket of orange smog, unlike any other moon!

e: Brilliant mathematician Emmy Noether proved that nature's beautiful symmetries keep energy and momentum perfectly balanced forever.

e: Gauss's law imagines wrapping charges in a magic bubble to count the electric field lines bursting out!

e: Coils resist changes in current with a magnetic hug, measured by a polite unit called the henry!

e: Matter is built from a fun little family of exactly six quirky quarks dancing inside every atom!

e: The shy graviton is supposed to carry gravity's pull, but no scientist has ever caught one peeking out!

e: Shining like a cozy flame, the candela measures brightness just like a single glowing birthday candle!
